top_issues: Conifer trees look like low-poly geometric cones with black, crushed interiors and severe alpha/normal artifacts on the fringes.
Water looks murky and olive-opaque rather than crystal-clear Sierra creek water showing warm, rocky stream beds underneath (compare to ref5/ref6).
Water shoreline intersection has an unnatural, blurry white/grey halo fade (depth fade artifact) around submerged stones in wet_stones.
Granite boulders are too uniformly smooth, bubbly, and chalky white/grey; they lack sharp fracture planes, mineral speckles, and warm iron-oxide/tannin staining in the creek bed.
Ground trail dirt looks like smooth, featureless plastic/sand with zero pebbles, pine needles, duff, or micro-topography.
Sky is completely blown out to pure white due to heavy fog inscatter and low sun pitch, lacking the deep blue/warm horizon gradient of the High Sierra.
code_suggestions: gen.py (Trees/Foliage): Replace stacked cone geometry for pines with irregular branched clusters or proper billboard/alpha-card needle boughs, and add subsurface scattering + higher ambient occlusion floor in ue_main.py so tree interiors aren't pitch black.

ue_main.py (Water Material): Switch water to SingleLayerWater shading model (or remove the bright DepthFade shoreline opacity band) and add warm reddish-brown/ochre vertex/world-height color tinting to submerged creek-bed rocks (as seen in ref4, ref5, ref6).

gen.py (Granite & Cobbles): Add Voronoi/Worley fracture displacement and high-frequency salt-and-pepper noise to granite boulders so they look angular and crystalline rather than melted snow, and scatter dense small cobbles/gravel along the water's edge.

gen.py / ue_main.py (Terrain/Trail): Add high-frequency normal/bump noise, scattered pine needles, small granite grit, and dry grass tufts (like ref2) to break up the smooth CG sand look of the trail and banks.
